summary: The reduction itself is right and I judge the unbounded window LANDABLE: growth is one HashMap entry per (podId, incarnationId), incarnationId is minted once per DefaultIngest instance (DefaultIngest.java:69, `private final`, one per ingester process), and CommitRequest has exactly one production construction site (DefaultIngest.java:355, in-process), so the map grows with fleet RESTARTS per leader term, not with records, flushes, shards or indices, and no remote caller can seed it. Request rates are unchanged and if anything lower without eviction: answer() still issues at most one GET per distinct (epoch,sequence) per batch, bounded by retrying pods. Against that, the withdrawn bound was measured to survive a mutation that CLEARS the window at the threshold -- fleet-wide loss of the property this row exists to deliver -- so shipping it would have been worse than the documented gap. The corrected Sequencer.java sentence is TRUE and I measured it: replacing the three attribution conjuncts in IdempotencyWindow.answers with `true` fails SequencerDedupTest.aSegmentMatchingOnlyPARTOfTheTripleAnswersNOTHING (SequencerDedupTest.java:249), so the replay-answer path does match a retry against the Attribution. One caveat on the same sentence, not a finding: its second clause, 'what M4.10f will rebuild a successor's window FROM', sits awkwardly beside M4.10f's own notes, which say the slots come from the predecessor's checkpoint `pods` via crossFromCheckpoint under a ZERO-ADDITIONAL-REQUESTS constraint; it is defensible only for the uncheckpointed tail that applyChain already reads. Both baseline arguments check out arithmetically: staged added lines are 382 main + 697 test = 1079 exactly as size:M4.10d claims, DeltaReader (45) + Submission (28) = 73 as claimed, 1079-73 = 1006 as claimed, and CommitLog at 473 lines makes 'the 500-line limit forced it anyway' true; '~410 production' is really 382, an overstatement against the author's own interest. rounds:M4.10d states round 4's verdicts accurately (reviewer pass, test-reviewer changes-requested on the single major M4.10d-tr-18) and paraphrases its remedy faithfully against the recorded round_judgement. What blocks is one sentence: the archive row this commit ADDS asserts the bound it withdrew.

findings.summary: The M4.10d row added by this commit states 'The window is bounded and evicts oldest-by-pointer, which costs the evicted incarnation its idempotency and says so.' The staged code has no bound, no eviction and no MAX_SLOTS: IdempotencyWindow.java:33-39 says the opposite in the same commit ('IT IS UNBOUNDED, AND THAT IS A KNOWN GAP'), and M4.10g exists precisely because the bound was withdrawn. The row's own correction clause -- 'SPLIT TWICE UNDER REVIEW' -- enumerates M4.10e and M4.10f and asserts 'neither half is optional', naming exactly two splits; the third (M4.10g) and the withdrawal appear nowhere in the row. This is task-says-X-diff-does-Y in the one artifact a person consults for what M4.10d delivered.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED against the staged bytes: `grep -rn 'MAX_SLOTS\|evict' --include=*.java` over the staged tree returns nothing in sequencer/src/main, and IdempotencyWindow.applied (line 116-124) is the whole record path with no eviction call. Two concrete harms. (1) backlog-done.md's own header says 'Nothing reads this file but a person and check-commit-msg.sh' and that rows already shipped are not rewritten -- so a later session picking up M4.10g reads M4.10d's done row, finds the bound and its eviction policy described as delivered, and closes M4.10g as already-done; the window then stays unbounded permanently, which is the one outcome this round's trade was made to avoid. (2) The entire justification for landing an unbounded map is that the growth is DOCUMENTED; the primary per-task document asserts the growth is bounded, so an operator sizing the sequencer heap from the backlog reads a guarantee that does not exist while the map gains an entry per pod incarnation for the life of a leader term (1,000 pods restarting hourly over a 7-day term is ~168k retained entries, inferred not measured). Remedy is one sentence in the row: say the bound was written, withdrawn under review and split to M4.10g, matching the class javadoc this commit already wrote.
